Thus, death should be known to occur even on the first day after conception due to the entry of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) into the *kaṇikā* (pericarp) within twenty-four hours; likewise, death occurs on the third day due to the arising of the vital breath in the twelfth petal; similarly, on the sixth day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the eleventh petal; likewise, on the eleventh day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the tenth zodiacal petal; similarly, on the twenty-first day, due to the arising of the vital breath in the ninth zodiacal petal; and thus, on the thirty-sixth day, due to the successive arising of the vital breath in the eighth zodiacal petal.

Thus, at two months, the breath arises from the seventh zodiacal leaf; thus, at three months, from the sixth leaf due to the arising of the breath; thus, at four months, from the fifth due to the arising of the breath; thus, at six months, after twenty days, from the fourth leaf due to the arising of the breath; thus, at one year and a half, from the third due to the arising of the breath; at two years, after ten days, from the second due to the arising of the breath; at the third year, from the first due to the arising of the breath; and in the fourth year, there is no rule regarding the days, up until the limit of one hundred years from conception—this is the rule for the solar fatal signs (*sūryāriṣṭa*).

Just as with the sun, so too is there a rule regarding the lunar portents (*candrāriṣṭa*) due to the birth from the womb according to the divisions of the three qualities, such as *sattva* and the rest. Thus, it was stated by Īśvara in the *Kālottara*, in the section on the upward flow (*ūrdhvaśrotra*): "As is *vāmā*, so is *avāmā* and likewise *madhyamā*; at the end of three years, [there is] *makhādā*. Therefore, since there is a rule in some places even in the *Parasiddhānta*, this is the rule for the lunar and solar portents.

Thus, from one day up to three years, the death of a child—whether on the path of the Moon or the path of the Sun—is divided into one thousand and eighty distinct types according to the specific daily variation of death. There is no fixed rule here for those born from a womb regarding their *karman*;
rather, the number of breaths (*prāṇa*) is known through the flow of the channels (*nāḍī*) and the days of ill omen (*ariṣṭa*).

Therefore, the wheel of ill omen and the wheel of death [is determined] by the sequential abandonment of the five-maṇḍala flow of the vital breath from the channels of the zodiacal signs (*rāśicakra*).

Then, the principle is that entry into the *kaṇikā* (the central point) signifies death on that very day. This characteristic of the three-year period refers to the death of all sentient beings as taught by the Blessed One, based on the calculation of the sun’s movement through the *madhyamā* flow within the limit of a hundred years.
That same [calculation] applies to the moon; however, by means of the moon's three-fortnightly cycle, there would be no untimely death (*ariṣṭa-maraṇa*) for the moon itself.

In this context, that by which death as an ill omen (*ariṣṭamaraṇa*) does not occur for the Moon is imagined by the ignorant and unawakened; for instance, they claim there is no death as an ill omen in the left channel due to the nature of the Moon, while death as an ill omen is taught by the Omniscient One to occur in the right [channel] due to the flow of the Sun. This is the statement of the ignorant. Here, the deity presiding over the three years is the "Sun" (prāṇa-vāyu), and the deity presiding over the three fortnights is the "Moon" (apāna-vāyu).

Prāṇa, the sun, is the presiding lord of the iḍā, piṅgalā, and suṣumnā; it flows upward from the navel. Apāna, the lord of the channels of feces, urine, and the moon, flows downward from the navel. This is the great section on the severance of the channels characterized by the signs of death (ariṣṭa).
Thus, below the moon are the three qualities, and above the sun are the five qualities corresponding to the five spheres.

Therefore, due to the division of the three qualities, the death-signs (ariṣṭa) of the moon occur in the left, and due to the division of the five qualities, the death-signs of the sun occur in the right—this is the rule for the death-signs of the moon and sun in the upper and lower channels.

Now, the characteristic of death at the full time of middle [life] is described by the verse beginning with "the year of time" (*kālābda*): For as long as one year of time, moving by the power of a daily motion, it ascends while transitioning into that which is called the Moon; on the path of the Sun, through an increase of one on alternate and even days, it gradually effects a further distinction of transits on alternate and even days within the twelve-spoked [wheel]. Indeed, for as long as a month and a half—namely, thirty [days] plus three nights—it constitutes the life span.

In this body of men and women, the flow of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) proceeds through the left and right channels by means of the five *maṇḍalas* for ninety-six years plus ten and a half months, according to the divisions of *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas*.
For humans with a lifespan of one hundred years, the rule is that the central time (*madhyamakāla*) lasts for three years and three fortnights.

In that regard, there are three channels—the left, right, and middle—which have the nature of *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas* respectively. Within these, Death, having taken hold of the count of the flow in the *tamas* channel, ascends through the left and right channels by means of the nature of *prāṇa* and *apāna* on uneven and even days, for a period of time consisting of years and three fortnights. By virtue of the movement of the days—namely, one thousand one hundred and twenty-five days—it ascends and migrates until the exhaustion of life occurs, moving through the left path called "Moon" and the right path called "Sun" on uneven and even days.

"By increase in sequence" means: if birth occurred in an odd sign such as Aries, it ascends through the left channel for one day; if birth occurred in an even sign such as Taurus, it ascends through the right for two days.

Thereafter, according to the measure of the days of ascent, it effects a further distinction of transits at the conclusion of the left ascent and at the conclusion of the right ascent by means of odd and even days.

In the twelve-spoked wheel of the zodiac, for the sake of gradually abandoning the five mandalas, he effects a transition (*saṃkrānti*) in the left channel for the purpose of exhausting the mandalas beginning with space, and in the right channel for the purpose of exhausting the mandalas beginning with earth.

Here, by ascending through five days on the left, the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) abandons the flow of the void mandala during the six transitions occurring in the six odd signs beginning with Aries; by ascending through six days on the right, the vital wind abandons the flow of the earth mandala during the six transitions occurring in the six even signs beginning with Taurus.
Thus, in eleven days, he abandons the wind-maṇḍala in the left channel; in twelve days, he abandons the water-maṇḍala in the right petals;
likewise, in seventeen days, he abandons the fire-maṇḍala in the left petals; in eighteen days, he abandons the fire-maṇḍala in the right petals;
furthermore, in twenty-three days, he abandons the water-maṇḍala in the left petals; and in twenty-four days, he abandons the wind-maṇḍala in the right petals.
Furthermore, in nineteen days he abandons the earth mandala in the six left petals;
in thirty days he abandons the space mandala in the right.
Thus, by ascending through odd and even days on the left and right, there is the abandonment of the five mandalas in the thirty channels of the twelve zodiacal signs over thirty days of transits.

Then, by ascending thirty-one days in the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*), there is the depletion of the *sattva* element in the odd petals; likewise, by ascending thirty-two days in the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*) over thirty-two transition days (*saṃkrānti*), there is the depletion of the *rajas* element.
Then, by ascending for thirty-three days, there is the depletion of the *tamas* constituent (*tamodhātu*) in the odd petals; that is, by thirty-three days of transits (*saṃkrānti*).

In this way, there is the depletion of the phlegm channel (*śleṣmanāḍī*); in the *Vimalaprabhā*, it is stated that the depletion of the sattva constituent (*sattvadhātu*) is the depletion of the bile channel (*pittanāḍī*), and the depletion of the wind channel (*vātanāḍī*) is the depletion of the *tamas* constituent (*tamodhātu*), occurring through the ascent of thirty-three days, that is, by thirty-three days of transits.

The days accumulated from the transits of both [solar] nodes amount to one thousand one hundred and twenty-two days, less three years, three fortnights, and three days; this is the severing of the channels of the *sattva*, *rajas*, and *tamas* of the five mandalas, which is the abandonment of the locations of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*).
Thus, for up to one and a half months, the days of the three years [are accounted for] by the ascent of the vital breath.

Then, another three-day period—the number of days and months of the embryonic stage consisting of thirty days, lasting up to three nights—is the ascent through the right channel; it is the absence of all transits for thirty-three days, during which there is the dissolution of the aggregates and elements.

In this context, there are the five aggregates beginning with form (*rūpa*), the five elements beginning with earth, the five sense organs beginning with the body organ, the five objects beginning with smell, the five action organs beginning with the anus, and the five objects of the action organs beginning with speech; the cessation of these—the absence of mutual conjunction—occurs over thirty-three days. Thereafter, for one day, they enter into the *madhyamā* for the purpose of exhausting the wheel of breaths.

The sixth aggregate (skandha), the sixth element (dhātu), the sixth sense-faculty (indriya), the sixth object (viṣaya), the sixth organ of action (karmendriya), and the object of the sixth organ of action—the emission of semen occurs at the end of death; such is the rule for the dissolution of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. Now, the ascent of the breaths at death for those born [into this world] is described by the verse beginning with "the breaths": "The breaths, the smeared [digits], the channels, the times of day and night, he ascends by way of transition; through seven years, through the limbs of the solstices, and by virtue of the movement of the solstices, through sixty years."
Thirty years, three months, and thirty-two fortnights, along with thirty-six and a half days, constitute the ascent from the Kālacakra according to the movement of the days and the years of time.
Here, in this body, the wheel of breaths, the wheel of *liptās*, the wheel of *ghaṭikās*, and the wheel of days exist just as they do externally, so too within the body.

In this regard, there is the wheel of breath (*śvāsacakra*) consisting of six breaths, the wheel of *pāṇīpala* consisting of sixty *pāṇīpala*s, and the wheel of *ghaṭikā*s consisting of sixty *ghaṭikā*s; furthermore, there is the wheel of *ariṣṭa* consisting of one thousand and eighty days, and the wheel of the days of timely death (*kālamṛtyudinacakra*) consisting of one thousand one hundred and fifty-six days. Within these wheels, death ascends through the left channel (*vamanāḍī*) and the right channel (*dakṣiṇanāḍī*) respectively in the form of breath, in the nature of *pāṇīpala*, in the nature of *ghaṭikā*, and in the nature of days, increasing by one at each stage;
first, it ascends as breaths.

Regarding the statement "by seven years from the mark of the solstice (*ayanāṅka*)," for one born here who has no fatal sign (*ariṣṭa*) up to the limit of a hundred years and whose death will not be timely, the life-force (*prāṇavāyu*) that carries the five spheres flows through both the left and right channels during two solstices.

Then, in the third solstice, it ascends by one breath into the space-sphere (*ākāśamaṇḍala*) in the left channel; in the fourth, it does not ascend. Then, in the fifth solstice of the third year, it ascends by two breaths into the earth-sphere (*pṛthivīmaṇḍala*) in the right channel; again, in the sixth solstice, it does not ascend.
Then, in the seventh transit (*ayana*), at Rohiṇī,
there are three years' worth of days (*trivarṣa-dināni*).
One should fashion twenty wheels for the sake of the goal.
The meaning of "aggregate" (*skandha*) is from the [Sanskrit] *aṅgāt* ("from a limb").
By means of [the signs occurring] after three years and so forth;

and that [is explained] in the chapter on the Great Summary of the Signs of Death and the Cessation of the Channels (*ariṣṭamaraṇalakṣaṇanāḍīcchedamahoddeśa*). On the left channel, at the sphere of space, the breath ascends three times during the eighth [year];
likewise, on the ninth [year], on the right channel, at the sphere of earth, the breath ascends four times during the tenth [year].
Furthermore, in the eleventh [year], one ascends five breaths in the void-maṇḍala in the left channel; in the twelfth, none;

and in the thirteenth year, one ascends six breaths in the earth-maṇḍala in the right channel during the southern transit (ayanam). In the fourteenth year, none. Thus, by means of these six breaths, that single wheel becomes one liptā or one pāṇīpala; herein lie seven years less half a month.
Therefore, for one who is not smeared [by the lunar days], there is no ascent of the breaths above;
rather, by virtue of being smeared, one ascends through the nature of the *liptās* due to the movement of the solstices over sixty years.
Thus, from seven years onwards until another sixty years, during the alternating solstices, one ascends by means of one day and so forth, increasing the odd *pāṇīpala*s.

Up to fifty-nine *liptās* in the left channel within the space-maṇḍala, and up to sixty *pāṇīpala*s—equalized by means of the second [day] and so forth—in the earth-maṇḍala of the right channel, across six petals each, which possess the nature of the odd and even *lagnas*, there is the wheel of *pāṇīpala*s consisting of sixty *pāṇīpala*s; that itself constitutes one *ghaṭikā*.
Therefore, up to the limit of sixty-seven years, the channel ascends by way of the nature of the death-channel (*mṛtyunāḍī*).

"Thirty years and three months"—this means that beginning again from a single channel (*nāḍī*), one ascends through the left and right channels by alternating between the odd and even channels. During half of the solstice (*ayanārddha*), for three months, one ascends one channel in the left channel within the space-maṇḍala (*ākāśamaṇḍala*). For the other three months, and again during the other half of the solstice for three months, one ascends two channels in the right channel within the earth-maṇḍala (*pṛthivīmaṇḍala*).

Thus, in three months, one ascends sixty channels in the left and right [channels] across the six zodiacal sectors (*rāśidala*)—namely, the space-maṇḍala and the earth-maṇḍala. Death occurs by the very nature of these channels.
Therefore, up until the limit of eighty-nine years minus one-and-a-half months, the wheel of nāḍīs ascends; that itself becomes one day.

Then, by way of the nature of the day, the wheel of days ascends through the left and right nāḍīs according to the previously mentioned sequence. Thus, by virtue of the movement of the days, and by means of time-years, fortnights, three-year periods—and by the word "and" (ca), by three-fortnight periods and thirty intercalary days—the number of days for the ascent of death is derived from the Kālacakra by dividing [the total] by thirty-two and a half.
The number of days obtained from one thousand one hundred and twenty-five should be understood as extending up to the *kaṇikā* (the pericarp).

Here, the days of ascent obtained by means of a division of thirty-two and a half are thirty-four; the *ghaṭikās* are thirty-six; the *pāṇīpalas* are fifty-five; and there are two and a half breaths (*śvāsa*s). Among these, one day remaining in the *kaṇikā* should be understood as the left and right *ariṣṭa* (fatal signs).
The daily ascent increases by one *ghaṭikā*, and the final ascent occurs in the right channel (*nāḍī*); such is the rule for the death by time (*kālamṛtyu*).

Now, the severing of the channels (nāḍī) at the navel-cakra and other locations is described, beginning with the words "in each fortnight" (pakṣe): In each fortnight, nine hundred channels are severed in the navel-cakra; at each junction, the Fire-day (the Sun) abandons one channel. In the action-cakra (karmacakra) called the throat, he abandons the lunar-mansion channels day by day.

Within a month, he gradually abandons the fortnight situated in the Bindu; within a fortnight, he abandons the lunar station (śaśipada); and situated in the heart, he abandons the weekday-channels (vāranāḍī).

Here, at the navel, there are sixty channels (*nāḍī*) belonging to the twelve zodiac signs (*rāśi*), which carry the sixty mandalas. Eight snakes multiplied by nine become seventy-two; thus, in the navel wheel (*nābhicakra*), one channel is severed every fortnight (*pakṣa*). Here, a fortnight should be understood as eighteen days. By that fortnight, the channel carrying the mandala beginning with space (*śūnya*) flows in the left.
In the *Vimalaprabhā*, it is stated that one abandons thirty channels over three years; on the right side, one abandons thirty channels that carry the mandalas beginning with Earth.

Thus, by means of thirty-three fortnights, sixty [channels] are abandoned by the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) throughout all the mandala-channels, having abandoned a sixth part. By means of the fortnights of the three years, one abandons the channel that carries the five mandalas.
It flows through each individual channel, abandoning them over the days of the sun (thirty) in the wheel of action known as *kriyā*.

Here, in this body, the wheel of action consists of twelve wheels divided into twelve parts according to the division of the twelve months, located in the six joints of the hands and the six joints of the feet.

In each individual joint-wheel there are thirty channels (*nāḍī*); thus, in the twelve joints, there are three hundred and sixty channels. Among these, in the joint of the right shoulder and arm, during the month of *Makara*, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days (*tithi*); in the joint of the left shoulder and arm, during the month of *Phālguna*, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days. Likewise, in the joint of the right upper arm, there are the channels of *Caitra*; in the joint of the left upper arm, the channels of *Vaiśākha*; in the joint of the right forearm, the channels of *Jyeṣṭha*; and in the joint of the left forearm, there are thirty channels according to the division of the thirty lunar days of *Āṣāḍha*.

In the two hands, at the karma-cakra, there are one hundred and eighty channels in the six types [of joints]; from there, in the six joints, thirty channels are in the joint of the right thigh and hip according to the lunar dates of the month of Śrāvaṇa,
and thirty channels are in the joint of the left thigh and hip for the month of Bhādrapada.
Thus, there are thirty channels at the junction of the right thigh and knee belonging to Aśvinī;
thirty channels at the junction of the left thigh and knee belonging to Kārttikī; and thirty channels at the junction of the right foot and knee belonging to Mārgaśīrṣā.
In the joint of the left knee, there are thirty channels by virtue of the nature of the thirty lunar days of the month of Puṣya;
thus, in the six joints of the two feet within the wheel of action (karmacakra), there are one hundred and eighty channels.
The wheel of action is that which serves as the basis for the initiation of the activities of the organs of action (karmendriya).

In these channels (*nāḍī*), by ascending through three days at a time starting from the day of the *śikhin* (the first day of the lunar fortnight), the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) abandons the three hundred and sixty channels over these one thousand and eighty days of the three years. This occurs in what is called the "Action" (*kriyā*) [cycle]. It is called "Action" because it performs actions such as taking up and moving; it consists of sixty joints (*parvan*) of the fingers and toes of the hands and feet. In each joint resides a wheel (*cakra*) composed of six channels, whose nature consists of the channels of earth, water, fire, air, void, and gnosis (*jñāna*). Thus, it is composed of six channels in each joint.
At the sixty joint-junctions, there are three hundred and sixty channels (*nāḍī*);
he abandons each individual channel every three days, just as in the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*).
When he abandons thirty channels at the joint of the right forearm, then he abandons six channels in each of the five upward-pointing fingers of the right hand.
Thus, one abandons thirty channels in the five fingers over the days of the month, which are the lunar dates (*tithi*);
this should be understood to apply to the left side as well.
When [the breath] abandons the joint of the right upper arm and forearm, it then abandons thirty channels in the joints of the middle phalanges of the fingers.
Likewise on the left side as well:

when [the breath] abandons the joint of the right shoulder and arm, it then abandons thirty channels in the joints of the fingers and below for thirty days; thus, in ninety days, it is to be understood that the same occurs on the left side as well.
When he abandons thirty channels at the joint of the right knee, then he abandons thirty channels at the joints of the half-joints of the toes of the right foot over the course of thirty days;
likewise on the left side as well.
When he abandons them at the joint of the right knee, then he abandons thirty channels at the middle joints of the toes.
In this same way, it should be understood for the left foot as well:
when [the breath] leaves the joint of the right hip and thigh, it then leaves thirty channels in the joints of the lower phalanges of the toes;
thus it should be understood for the left as well.

Now, the presiding deities and phonemes of the channels (*nāḍī*) are described: here, the *ka*-group, differentiated by the short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*) in reverse order, is located at the joint of the left shoulder and arm;
likewise, at the joint of the right shoulder and arm, the *ka*-group is differentiated by the long measures (*dīrghamātrā*) beginning with knowledge (*jñāna*).

At the joint of the left upper arm and forearm, the *ca*-group is differentiated by the short measures beginning with space; at the right [joint], it is differentiated by the six long measures beginning with knowledge.

On the left, the *ṭa*-group, non-different from the six measures beginning with space (*ākāśa*), resides at the joints of the hands and forearms; on the right, likewise the six months [of the northern solstice], non-different from the measures beginning with gnosis (*jñāna*). Thus, regarding the cutting of the channels (*nāḍīccheda*) as a sign of imminent death (*ariṣṭamaraṇa*) during the great summer solstice (*mahohairā*) in the northern course (*uttarāyaṇa*): thereafter, at the joint of the right hip and thigh, the *pa*-group, non-different from the six long measures beginning with gnosis, is on the right; on the left, it is non-different from the short measures beginning with space.

Thus, at the right knee-joint, there is the *tavarga* (the group of *t*, *th*, *d*, *dh*, *n*) differentiated by the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna* (knowledge); on the left, it is differentiated by the six short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*).

Likewise, at the right ankle-joint, there is the *savarga* (the group of *s*, *sh*, *ṣ*, *s*, *h*) differentiated by the six long vowels beginning with *jñāna*; on the left, it is differentiated by the six short vowels beginning with space, starting from the consonant of space in reverse order.

In this way, each group consists of thirty syllables through the distinction of long and short vowels; thus, they reside in the twelve wheels of the *karmacakra* (action wheel), which has thirty spokes.
Then, within the wheels of action (*kriyā-cakra*), each consonant beginning with *ka* is conjoined with the six long vowels (*jñānādi*) starting from [the vowel *ā*].

At each joint, beginning from the right thumb—specifically at the joint below the thumb, which consists of six channels—the consonant *ka* is conjoined with the six long vowels starting from *jñāna*. At the joint of the index finger is the letter *kha*; at the joint of the middle finger is *ga*; at the joint of the ring finger is *gha*; and at the joint of the little finger is *ṅa*, conjoined with the six long vowels starting from *jñāna*.

At the joint of the lower phalanx of the left little finger is the letter *ṅa*, distinguished by the six short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*); at the joint of the ring finger is *gha*; at the joint of the middle finger is *ga*; at the joint of the index finger is *kha*; and at the joint of the thumb is *ka*, distinguished by the six short vowels beginning with space. Thus, in the second row of phalanges on the right hand, beginning from the thumb, is the *ca*-group (*cavarga*), distinguished by the long vowels; on the left, it is distinguished by the short vowels. Likewise, in the third row of phalanges on the right hand is the *ṭa*-group (*ṭavarga*), distinguished by the long vowels; on the left, it is distinguished by the short vowels.

Thus, on the joints of the toes of the right foot, the *pa*-group (*pavarga*) is divided by long vowels; on the left, it is divided by short vowels. On the middle joints of the right [hand], the *ta*-group (*tavarga*) is divided by long vowels; on the left, it is divided by short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*). On the upper joints of the right [hand], the *sa*-group (*savarga*) is divided by long vowels; on the joints of the left fingers, it is divided by the six vowels beginning with space in reverse order. This refers to the first year. In the second [year], they are divided by the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions; in the third, the six groups are divided by the *yaṇādeśa* and other such operations.
The detailed explanation of this will be stated in what follows, so it is not elaborated upon here:
"Day by day, within a month, he gradually abandons the channels of the lunar mansions in the throat.
This means that in the throat-cakra, there are channels for the twenty-eight lunar mansions; he abandons them over twenty-eight days, which consist of the vowels.

The lunar station situated at the *bindu* and located in the forehead, consisting of fourteen channels, is abandoned in the middle of the fortnight over fourteen days by means of the fourteen *pluta* vowels;

the channel of the weekday is abandoned in eight days by means of the qualities such as the objects and the *sattva*, etc.; and the thirty consonant-natured channels situated in the secret place are abandoned at the time of death—such is the rule for the severance of the channels.

Now, regarding the cutting off of the forward and reverse movement of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) within the wheels of action by means of its solar nature, the [movement] of the channels is described through the designations of the groups (*varga*), beginning with the words "from the groups": "The Sun moves from the groups together with the vowels according to the divisions of the zodiac signs for the duration of a solstice (*ayana*); afterwards, day by day, he moves in reverse by one [sign] each until the year of time is reached.

When the year is cut short, in the middle of the fortnight, there is ascent and descent by virtue of the days of the vowels; and at the time of day and night, there is the loss of inhalation and exhalation, resulting in the life-span being reduced by a single night. (68)

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, regarding the inner [system]: here, in the wheel of action (*karmacakra*) with twelve spokes, there are wheels consisting of thirty channels (*nāḍī*) at each of the twelve joints of the hands and feet. Within those twelve wheels, which are presided over by the thirty lunar days beginning with the month of Māgha, the six groups of consonants beginning with *ka*—distinguished by the six long vowels beginning with the visarga—are situated in the six joints of the right hand and feet according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), by way of the phonetic properties of the consonants starting with *pṛthivī* (earth). Likewise, the six groups of consonants, distinguished by the short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*), are situated in the six joint-wheels of the left hand and feet according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*), following the recitation of the *pratyāhāra* beginning with *ṅ*.

The sun moves through those classes [of letters] along with their vowels, together with the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) and death, through the solstice (*ayana*) by means of the divisions of the zodiac signs. The first solstice is the northern course (*uttarāyaṇa*), beginning with Capricorn (*makara*) and the month of Māgha; that very same solstice revolves through the six junction-wheels (*sandhicakra*) of the right and left arms.

Likewise, in the *kriyācakra*, within the thirty finger-joint wheels (*parvasandhi-cakra*) consisting of six channels each, the consonants beginning with *ka*—distinguished by the six long vowels—move through the wheel of each individual finger-joint in the joints of the fingers of the right hand according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*). In the left [hand], the consonants beginning with *ha* (representing space, etc.)—distinguished by the vowels beginning with *ā* (space, etc.)—move according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*). Thus, the southern course occurs in the six joint-wheels of the feet known as the *karmacakra*, while it occurs in the finger-joints known as the *kriyācakra*.

In this context, during the month of Māgha at the Makara-saṃkrānti, the moon is to be understood according to the variation of lunar dates (*tithi*), and the sun’s ascent according to the variation of the day of the week (*vāra*) of the transit.
Where the sun increases, there is a waning of the moon; where the moon increases, there is a waning of the sun.

Thus, at the beginning of Capricorn (*makara*), there is an increase of the sun. In Capricorn, within the thirty channels (*nāḍī*) of the wheel at the joint of the right shoulder and arm, there are the thirty consonants beginning with *ka*, differentiated by long vowels.

The presiding deities (adhidevatās) are those whose nature is perception (*saṃjñā*), while [the letters] are those whose nature is vital breath (*prāṇa*). Thus, in the first channel (*nāḍī*) there are *kkāḥ*;

likewise, in each of the three joints of all the fingers and toes, there are syllables in their respective order. For example: *kkāḥ*, *kklū*, *kkū*, *kkṝ*, *kkī*, *kkā*—these are in the six channels of the first set of six channels at the joint below the thumb of the right hand in the wheel of action (*kriyācakra*).

Similarly, *khāḥ*, *khkh*, *khkhū*, *khṝ*, *khkhī*, *khkhā* are in the six channels at the joint below the index finger in the wheel of action (*kriyācakra*), which is the second set of six channels in the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*).

Likewise, *ggāḥ gglū ggū ggre ggaggī ggā* are in the six channels of the third [spoke] of the Karmacakra; in the Kriyācakra, at the joint below the middle finger, they are in the six channels as *ṅaṅa* in the six channels. Similarly, *dhghāḥ ghghlū ghghū ghṛ ghdhī ghghā* are in the six channels of the fourth [spoke] of the Karmacakra; in the Kriyācakra, at the joint below the ring finger, they are in the six channels.

Thus, in the fifth *karmacakra*, there are six channels (*nāḍī*) with [the syllables] ṅ, ṅāḥ, ṅ, ṅa, ṅa, ṅī, and ṅṅā; likewise, in the *kriyācakra*, at the joint of the lower phalanx of the little finger, there are six channels.
In this manner, the Sun abandons each mandala—earth and the others—by means of six days each;
in thirty days, it abandons the five mandalas. Thereafter, it transits into Aquarius (*kumbha*) in the left channel (*vāmanāḍī*).
In that regard, the sequence beginning with space (ākāśa) is the *ka*-group in the action-wheel (*karmacakra*) known as "activity" (*kriyā*).

Here, during the month of Phālguna or at the transit of the Sun into Aquarius (*kumbhasaṃkrānti*), in the action-wheel at the joint of the left shoulder and arm, within the thirty channels (*nāḍī*), there are the consonants beginning with *ṅa*, differentiated by the short vowels beginning with space (*ākāśa*), [representing] the spheres (*maṇḍala*) of space and so forth. For example: *ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa ṅa*—these are in the six channels of the first group, characterized by the six spheres beginning with space, in the wheel of activity (*kriyācakra*) at the joint of the lower phalanx of the left little finger.

Thus, *gha gha ghṛ ghughla ghaṃ*— these are in the six channels of the second wind-maṇḍala within the wheel of one's own activity (*svakarmacakra*), specifically in the six channels at the joint below the ring finger of the wheel of action (*kriyācakra*).
Likewise, *ga gi gṛ gu glū gaṃ*— these are in the six channels of the third fire-maṇḍala, starting with *ka kha*.
The phrase "with those beginning with the letter ma" does not exist in the Ga manuscript.
It is not in manuscript kha.

Thus, in the chapter on the *gati*, the great section on the signs of death and the cessation of the channels (*ariṣṭamaraṇalakṣaṇa-nāḍīccheda-mahoddeśa*), concerning the wheel of karma and its activity: at the joints of the lower segments of the middle [channel], there are six channels.
Thus, in these six channels, there is the fourth water mandala: *kha*, *khi*, *khṛ*, *khla*, *khaṃ*.
In the *karmacakra* and the *kriyācakra*, at the joint below the ring finger (*tarjanī*), there are six channels (*nāḍī*);

likewise, *ka, ki, kṛ, ku, kula, kaṃ* reside in the six channels of the earth-maṇḍala in the fifth [finger] of the *karmacakra*. In the *kriyācakra*, the six measures (*mātrā*) of the letter *ka* reside in the six channels at the first joint below the thumb.

Thus, during one season, in the right and left [hands], in the months of Capricorn (*makara*) and Aquarius (*kumbha*), the sixty measures and so forth occur according to the distinction between withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*).
Then, from the *ca*-group, which consists of six measures, he moves through the right arm and forearm joints by means of the divisions of Pisces and Aries;
and in the thirty channels (*nāḍīs*) of the five mandalas beginning with Earth, he moves through the *ca*-group together with its vowels according to the division of six days.
The process of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) is as follows: *ccāḥ, cclū, ccū, ccū, ccī, ccā* [in the element] Earth.
Chchā, chch, chchū, chchū, chchī, chchā—thus in water.
Jjāḥ, jjlū, jjū, jj, jjī, jjā—thus in fire.
Jhhāḥ, jhjhḷ, jhūjhū, jhajhajhajhī, jhjhā—thus in wind.
*Ñña, ñña, ñña, ññī, ñña*—these are in space (*ākāśa*).

Thirty *mātrās* are to be known in the action-wheel (*karmacakra*) and also in the activity-wheel (*kriyācakra*), as thirty letters beginning with *ca*, in the five joints from the middle phalanx of the right thumb to the middle phalanx of the little finger, and in the six channels (*nāḍīs*), according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*).

Thus, at the joint of the left upper arm and forearm in the *karmacakra*, there are thirty channels; and likewise, in the *kriyācakra*, from the middle joint of the little finger to the end of the middle joint of the thumb, there are thirty syllables beginning with *tra* in the six sets of six channels across the five joints. They are as follows: *ña ñi ñū ñṛ ñḷ ñaṃ* in the sphere of space (*ākāśamaṇḍala*);
*jhajhi jha jhu jhṛ jhḷ jhaṃ* in wind (*vāyu*); *jaji jṛ ju jḷ jaṃ* in fire (*tejas*).
*Cha, chi, chṛ, chu, chl, chaṃ*—thus in water;
*ca, ci, cu, cla, caṃ*—thus in earth.
In this manner, during the spring season, the *ca*-group proceeds according to the division of the zodiac signs.

Then, at the joint of the right forearm with the hand, in the *karmacakra*, he traverses the thirty channels; and in the five joints beginning from the upper phalanx of the right thumb, in the six sets of six channels, he traverses the *ṭa*-group according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) by means of the divisions of the bull.
It is as follows: *ṭṭāḥ, ṭūla, ṭū, ṭṭu, ṭṭī, ṭṭā* on earth;
*ṭhṭhāḥ, laṭhṭha, ṭha, ṭhṭhī, ṭhṭhā* in water.
Ḍḍāḥ, ḍḍḷ, ḍḍḍū, ḍḍḍa, ḍḍī, ḍḍā—these are in fire; ḍhḍhāḥ, ḍh, ḍhḍhū, ḍhar̤ha, ḍhḍhī, ḍhḍhā—these are in air;
ṇṇāḥ, ṇa, ṇṇū, ṇṇū, ṇṇī, ṇṇā—these are in ether.
Thus by way of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*).

Then, by way of emanation (*sṛṣṭi*), in the left upper arm-joint at the *karmacakra*, within the thirty channels; and in the *kriyācakra*, within the six channels at the joints of the upper phalanges of the left little finger up to the thumb phalanges, there are the syllables beginning with *ṇa* according to the sequence of the spheres (*maṇḍala*) starting from space (*ākāśa*).
They are as follows: *ṇa, ṇi, ṇū, ṇu, ṇ, ṇaṃ* in space.
Ḍha, ḍhi, ḍṛ, ḍa, ḍa, ḍu, ḍla, ḍaṃ are in the wind;
ḍa, ḍi, ḍa, ḍu, ḍla, ḍaṃ are in fire;
ṭha, ṭhi, ṭha, ṭhu, ṭhūla, ṭhaṃ are in water.
"Ṭa-ṭi-ṭṭa ṭu ṭulu ṭaṃ"— thus,
during the summer season, the Sun moves through the divisions of the zodiac signs by means of the bull and its consort;
in this manner, during the northern transit (uttarāyaṇa), the Sun traverses one hundred and eighty syllables through the divisions of the zodiac signs throughout the course of the transit.

"Afterwards, it ascends one [digit] more each day" means that subsequently, during the southern transit (*dakṣiṇāyana*), when the moon—the *apāna* wind—is present, death ascends; the sun ascends and becomes diminished. During the night of the moon, there is an increase; according to the principle that "death ascends through the steps of that which increases," the sun ascends from the hands, fingers, head, and joints, [consisting of] the *ka-kha* measures; *ga* measures; the collection of signs (*rāśi*).
The zodiac sign (*rāśi*) moves like the sun; it does not become diminished (*na hīno bhavati*).
*Bho.*: "It does not become base" (*dman par mi hgur*).
At night—
according to the *Vimalaprabhā* on the inner [system]— up until the first channel of the joint between the right shoulder and the upper arm.
Here, during the southern solstice, the moon moves, entering the channels at the joint of the right hip and thigh in the wheel of karma (*karmacakra*).

From the lower joint of the right thumb to the lower joint of the little finger, by way of the process of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), thirty letters of the *p*-group move through the six channels at each of the five finger-joint articulations within the *kriyācakra*. By means of the Cancer division, he is the lord of three years;
namely: *ppāḥ ppla ppū ppū ppī ppā* on earth, and *phphāḥ phphlū phphū phpha phphī phphā* on water.
bbāḥ bblū bbū bbū bbī bbā in fire;
bhbhāḥ bhbhla bhbhū bhū bhī bhbhā in wind;
mmāḥ mm mmū mm mmī mmā in space.
Thus, by means of the division of Cancer (*karkaṭa*).

Then, at the joint of the left hip and thigh, according to the sequence of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*) and by means of the division of the mandalas beginning with space (*ākāśa*), there are thirty syllables in reverse order; namely: *ma mi mṛ mu mlṛ maṃ* for space.
*bha bhi bhṛ bhu bhlṛ bhaṃ* for air;
*ba bi bṛ bu blū baṃ* for fire;
*pha phi phu phlu phaṃ* for water.
*Pa*, *pi*, *pṛ*, *pu*, *plū*, and *paṃ*—by means of the division of the lion transit (*siṃhasaṃkrānti*) on the earth, the month of Bhādrapada proceeds.
Thus the moon proceeds through the rainy season, while the sun recedes.

Then, at the joint of the right thigh and knee, in the karma-cakra and kriyā-cakra, from the middle joint of the big toe to the middle joint of the little toe, the *tavarga* (the *t*-group) proceeds through the six channels in the five joints; from those, thirty syllables [proceed] by way of the division of the withdrawal of the zodiac signs.
Namely: *ttāḥ ṭṭḷ ṭṭū ṭṭu ṭṭī ṭṭā* for earth;
*ththāḥ ththḷ ththyū ththyū ththī ththyā* for water;
*ddāḥ dṛddī ddā* for fire.
*Dhdhāḥ*, *dhḷ*, *dhdhū*, *dhdhṛ*, *dhdhī*, *dhdhā*—these [syllables] are in the wind;
*nnāḥ*, *nn*, *ntu*, *nnu*, *nnī*, *nnā*—these are in space.
Thus, the Moon moves according to the divisions of the Virgo (Kanyā) sign.

Then, at the junctions of the left thigh and knee—in the *karmacakra* or the *kriyācakra*—from the middle joint of the little toe of the left foot up to the big toe, in the six channels (*nāḍī*) at the five joints, they are as follows: *na, ni, nṛ, nu, nḷ, naṃ* for space (*ākāśa*);
likewise, *dha, dhi, dhṛ, dhu, dhḷ, dhaṃ* for air (*vāyu*); and similarly, *da, di, dṛ, du, dḷ, daṃ* for fire (*tejas*).
*Thathi thū thu thlṛ thaṃ*—thus [the moon] moves in water;
*ta ti tṛ tu tlṛ taṃ*—thus [it moves] on earth.

In this manner, by the division of the scales (*tulābheda*), the moon proceeds in the left [nostril] according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*), while the sun recedes during the autumn season.

Then, at the junction of the right knee in the *karmacakra*, within the thirty channels of the *kriyācakra*, the Moon traverses the thirty syllables of the *sa*-group along with their *mātrās* according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) and the division of the scorpion (*vṛścika*), from the upper joint of the right thumb to the upper joint of the little finger across the five joints in the six sets of six channels.
Meanwhile, the Sun ascends on the right side.
For example: *ssāḥ sslū ssū ssa ssī ssā* on the earth-maṇḍala.
*yyāḥ, yyyū, yyū, yyī, yyā* in water;
*ṣṣāḥ, ṣṣlṛ, ṣṣū, ṣṣū, ṣṣī, ṣṣā* in fire;
*śśāḥ, śśla, śśū, śśū, śśī, śśā* in air.
Thus, *kā klū kū kṛ kī kā*—these thirty syllables are [located] in the six channels in the space (*ākāśa*) according to the division of Scorpio (*vṛścika*).

Then, on the left leg, at the joint of the knee, in the karma-cakra, within the thirty channels of the action-cakra (*kriyā-cakra*), from the upper joint of the little finger up to the upper joint of the thumb, across the five joints of the five fingers, the Moon traverses the thirty syllables in the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭi-krama*) within the six sets of six channels.
The Sun, by means of the Sagittarius (*dhanuṣ*) division, exits from the shoulder-element in the left arm.
Namely: *ka ki kṛ ku kla kaṃ* in space;
likewise, *śa śi śṛ śu śla [śaṃ]* in wind;
*ṣa ṣi ṣṛ ṣu ṣla ṣaṃ* in fire;
*Yya, yyi, yyū, yyu, yyla, yyaṃ*—thus in water; likewise *sa, si, sṛ, su, sla, saṃ*—thus in earth;
thus there are thirty syllables according to the division of the bow.

Therefore, starting from the winter season (śiśira-ṛtu), there is an absence of the moon's movement. [In this] chapter, [it is stated that] the sun increases again at the beginning of Capricorn (makara). This is the great section on the signs of death (ariṣṭamaraṇa-lakṣaṇa) and the cutting of the channels (nāḍīccheda). Regarding "ka. kha. candraṃ": [this refers to the lunar cycle].

In the first year, time proceeds together with the sun and moon according to the divisions of the *sattva* quality; then, in the second year, the thirty consonants beginning with *ka*, categorized by the divisions of *rajas* and the vowels of the qualities and increments (*guṇavṛddhi*), are to be understood as before within the thirty channels of the action wheel (*karmacakra*) and the activity wheel (*kriyācakra*).
In Capricorn (*makara*), this occurs through the process of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*), as follows: *kkāḥ, kkāl, kkau, kkār, kkai, kkā* on earth (*avanī*);
likewise, *khkhāḥ, khkhāl, khkhī, khkhār, khkhai, khkhā* on water (*udaka*).
*ggāḥ ggāl ggauggār ggai ggā* in fire;
*ghghāḥ ghghār ghghau ghghār ghye ghghā* in wind;

*ṅṅāḥ ṅṅāl ṅṅau ṅṅār ṅa ṅā* in the sphere of space. As before, on the right arm, the sun moves by means of the division of Capricorn (*makara*); the moon moves out on the right foot; likewise, by means of the division of Aquarius (*kumbha*), it moves through the sequence of the qualities (*guṇa*) according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*).

In Cancer and Leo, at the junction of the quarters, within thirty *nāḍīs*, [the breath] moves through the thirty syllables of the vowels and consonants combined with the qualities of increase (*vṛddhi*) and modification (*guṇa*), as before, on the right and left. During the rainy season (*vārṣya-ṛtu*), the Moon moves through the syllables of the *pa*-group joined with the qualities of increase and modification; during autumn, the syllables of the *ta*-group; and during the cold season (*śiśira*), the syllables of the *sa*-group, according to the sequence of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*).
Thus, in the second year, the Moon and Sun move through three hundred and sixty *mātrās*.

Then, in the third year, Time moves together with the Sun through the consonant groups (*kādivarga*) along with their vowels by means of the piercing of darkness (*tamobheda*). Here, the vowels are said to be the *yaṇādeśas*; together with them, Time moves through thirty syllables for each [group], pertaining to the domain of darkness. This occurs, as before, through the distinction of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*) in the joints of the hands and feet, in the wheels of action (*karmacakra*) and the wheels of activity (*kriyācakra*).
For example: *kkhāḥ*, *kklā*, *kkvā*, *kkā*, *kkyā*, *kkhā*—thus on Earth, by way of the Makara division.

Likewise, *khkhhā*, *khlā*, *rūkhvā*, *khkhā*, *khkhyā*, *khkhhā* [occur] in water; likewise, *gahā*, *galā*, *gvā*, *ggrā*, *gayā*, *rahā* [occur] in fire; *ghghā*, *ghghlā*, *ghghvā*, *ghghrā*, *ghhyā*, *ghghhā* [occur] in wind; *ṅhā*, *ṅlā*, *ṅvā*, *ṅkā*, *ṅyā*, *ṅaṅhā* [occur] in space. Thus the sun moves through the right [side], and then through the left by way of the process of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*).
*Haṃ yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ* in the ether;
*ghha ghya ghra ghva ghla ghhaṃ* in the wind;
*gha gya gra gva gla gre* in the fire.
*Kh-kha-khra-khva-khla-khaṃ* in water;
*kha-ky-kra-kva-kla-khūṃ* in earth.
Thus, during the winter season (*śiśira*), the sun moves through thirty measures (*mātrā*) in the left [nostril] by way of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*).
Thus, during spring the *ca*-group [is predominant], and during summer the *ṭa*-group.
Thereafter, the sun moves upward from the six joints;
the moon moves through the joint of the feet.
O Vārṣṇeya, the labial class (*pavarga*) is as before;
the dental class (*tavarga*) is in autumn;
and the palatal class (*savarga*) is in winter, according to the distinctions of withdrawal and creation.

In this way, during the third year as well, the sun traverses exactly three hundred and sixty measures (*mātrā*). [End of] the Great Chapter on the Severing of the Channels (*nāḍīccheda*) as a Sign of Death and Misfortune. Now, the increase of time through the exhaustion of the movements of the moon and sun is stated, beginning with the words "by thirty-six," etc.: "By thirty-six thousand, the channel of time (*kālanāḍī*) grows for the total number of days in one hundred years—that which is filled by the respective movements of the sun and moon during the day and night. During the solar day, however, there is a debt in the solar movement, and half of that in the lunar movement."
In the division of days by the lunar mansions, the movement of the sun and moon is empty in the month of death.

In this context, when the number of days in a hundred years is calculated, there are thirty-six thousand days; this is designated as "dhru" (the fixed). By those thirty-six thousand days of the "dhru" count, the "time-channel" (*kālanāḍī*) arises. Death increases within the channels; the death-wind enters into seventy-two thousand [channels], and the five-maṇḍala wind gradually recedes, leaving behind a sixth part therein.
Which channel does the Kālanāḍī wind ascend?

Whichever [channel] is filled by the Sun and Moon during the day and night through their respective movements and the movement of the constellations—therein, the Sun is powerless due to the movement of the constellations, and the Moon is powerless due to the quarters of the lunar days (*tithi*).
In the movement of the Sun, there are twelve days; however, in the movement of the Moon, even for a moment, it would be half of that, namely six days.

In this regard, because the sun does not traverse one zodiac sign in thirty days every month, nor does the moon traverse sixty *daṇḍas*, the movement of the sun and moon proceeds through the divisions of the lunar days (*nakṣatrāha*) within the "empty month" (*śūnyamāsa*) of death. That empty month, at the end of thirty-two months, consists of sixty-four *nāḍīs*;

in those sixty-four *nāḍīs*, the wind of emptiness (*śūnyavāyu*) grows forth. Since two *nāḍīs* grow each day from among the seventy-two thousand [channels] in the navel-lotus, this is the general (gross) rule.

Now, the ascent by means of the division of breaths every day is described, beginning with the words "The vital breaths" (*prāṇā*): The vital breaths (*prāṇāḥ*) which are predominant in the body—sixty minus one-quarter of a Veda (fifty-seven and a half)—are all destroyed in each pair of channels (*nāḍī*) during the time of every daily solar transit (*saṃkrānti*), occurring again and again within a year due to the movement of the Sun and Moon through their quarters. Thus, in the number of zeros, eyes, and mountains (seven thousand two hundred), time passes for gods and men over a hundred years according to their respective measures of lifespan. (71)

Here, among the twenty-one thousand six hundred [breaths], those which flow through the mandala of gnosis (jñānamaṇḍala) are said to have authority over the breaths within the body when the equinox (viṣuva) is manifest between both junctions (lagna). This amounts to sixty-four and a quarter, or fifty-six and three-quarters. All of these, becoming one hundred seventy-five channels (puṭa) through the divisions of the twelve transits (saṃkrānti), destroy a pair of channels at every daily occasion; such is the reading of the scripture. The form of the verb used is *ghnantī* ("they kill").
This pair of channels—among the seventy-two thousand channels on the left and right—is destroyed. This results in the destruction of the movement of the winds of the five *maṇḍalas*.

Thus, forty-five breaths remain, which recur repeatedly within the year. In this way, as two channels are destroyed each day, by the days of the year (three hundred and sixty days) within the year, through the movement of the sun and moon's feet—the circulation of the right and left *maṇḍalas*—above that [point], there is the "sixty-part" (*ṣaṣṭyaṃśa*).
Ka. "The breaths and so forth" (śvāsādikā); kha. "In the east, the number of eyes and mountains" (śūnyanetrādrisaṃkhyā) means seven hundred and twenty.

Thus, time passes for gods and humans by thirty-six thousand years and one thousand days; or rather, it consists of seventy-two thousand nāḍīs that carry the five maṇḍalas, which is the movement of the moon and sun according to their respective measures as previously stated—by means of the days of the subtle body, the elements, the deities, and so forth. This is the rule for the cutting off of the nāḍīs.

Now, the nature of the *kālanāḍī* is described with the words beginning "If bitten," and so forth: "If a bite, a disease, or a blow should ever occur to men during the *kālanāḍī*, then by means of that [cause], Time suddenly enters the root-chakras.
Having blocked the channels in the chakras and having severed the entire movement of the sun and moon, O Lord of Men, it seizes the life of living beings, which rests in the subtle center. (72)

In this body, when the breath flows through the central channel (madhyamā) at the time of Kāla-nāḍī, if a person is bitten, falls ill, or is struck by a blow, then immediately and suddenly, through that very support, the wind of Time (Kāla), which is like a great darkness, enters the six root-chakras.

And having entered, he blocks the one hundred and fifty-six channels within the six wheels; having severed the movement of the sun and moon in the left and right channels, he seizes that life—the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*)—which is entirely dependent on the center and rests in the *avadhūtī* channel, O King, for this is the rule of the time-channels regarding the life of living beings.

Now, the movements of the moon at the beginning of the turning of the wheel of Dharma are described, starting with "in the heart-lotus" and so forth: In the heart-lotus and the illustrious forehead, the lunar station moves for a period known as the elements (5), the directions (10), and the days (7). In the *saṃbhoga* [wheel], it moves in the navel-wheel for a period of nine plus ten (19) and Rudra (11) doubled (22), which is called the *jina* [station].

Having stayed for seven nights, this moon, which is the *bindu*, abandons that station; then, ascending again in the bright fortnight, it enters the heart in due order, having first filled the *bindu*.

In this system, the increase or decrease of the lunar days (*tithi*) occurs through the even or odd progression of the moon’s movement by means of its fourteen-fold division of its steps (*caraṇa*); that [increase or decrease] on the seventh day, across seven lunar days, multiplied by the five objects of the senses (twenty-five), ceases on the seventh day—whether as increase or decrease—once one hundred and twenty steps have been completed according to the divisions of the infant, the youth, and so forth.

Here, the one hundred and twenty parts are described: when one foot is observed remaining as fourteen parts here, five parts of the sixty *nāḍikā*-parts of the *kalā* of that day become added to the wealth (*dhana*) of the *kalā*; on the second day, five parts of the second [foot] are [added], while those of the first [foot] are to be known as doubled through the division of the Kumāra [period]—[this applies] to the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇā*) or the light fortnight (*śuklā*) in the place of debt (*ṛṇasthāna*). [This is stated] in Ka. Kha.; [the term] *tanuja* in Bhoṭa; [and] in Ka. Kha.
it is "possessing that" (*tadvati*).
Ka. Kha. 0 Varaṇā. [In the] Paṭala [entitled] "The Great Chapter on the Signs of Death through Ariṣṭa and the Severing of the Channels":
thus, on the third day, there are five parts of the third [channel]; likewise ten of the second; and fifteen by the division of the first [wind].
Thus, by the division of the child (bāla), there are five parts of the fourth, ten of the third, fifteen of the second, and nineteen of the first by the division of the youth (yuvan).
Thus, on the fifth day: five parts for the fifth [tithi], ten for the fourth, fifteen for the third; nineteen for the second, and twenty-two for the first according to the *vṛddha* division.

Likewise, on the sixth day: five parts for the sixth, ten for the fifth, fifteen for the fourth, nineteen for the third, twenty-two for the second, and twenty-four for the first according to the *ativṛddha* division.

Thus, on the seventh day, there are twenty-five parts: five from the seventh [tithi], ten from the sixth, fifteen from the fifth, nineteen from the fourth, twenty-two from the third, and twenty-four from the second; and by the division of the state of ripening (*pakvāvasthā*), twenty-five parts from the first [tithi] become either wealth or debt according to the movement of the feet (*caraṇa*). In this manner, the measurement for all [tithis] is to be known through the sequence beginning with the "infant" (*bāla*) and so forth.

Thus, having taken the degrees of the seven lunar days (*tithis*), the Moon moves through the one hundred and twenty petals of the heart-lotus and other centers; thereafter, it moves upward again, returning to its own station—the meaning being that it returns to the "foot of the Moon.

Specifically, there are eight degrees in the eight petals of the heart, sixteen degrees in the sixteen petals of the throat (*ṣoḍaśāra*), thirty-two degrees in the thirty-two petals of the Sambhoga center, and sixty-four degrees in the sixty-four petals of the navel-lotus.
Thus, after consuming one hundred and twenty parts, the waning or waxing of the lunar digit ceases.

In the heart-lotus and the forehead, [the moon] abandons that which is called the elements (5), the directions (10), and the days (7); in the throat (sambhoga) and the navel, it abandons that which is known as the Rudras (11) with nine and ten added (21), and that which is called the principles (24).
This moon, as it ascends upward, abandons these in seven nights.

Twenty-five parts of the first digit (kalā) become fully ripened; that [digit], on the eighth day, becomes the presiding deity of the navel. Then, on the full moon day, it makes [the digits] complete in the navel, heart, throat, and forehead, having completed the full digit in the location of the drop (bindu). Thereafter, ascending again from the navel, there are sixty-four parts in the sixty-four petals, eight parts in the heart, thirty-two parts in the throat, and sixteen parts in the forehead; thus, in fourteen days, the completion of the stages (padāni) occurs.
Having performed the *pūrṇāhuti* in that [navel], he enters the heart during the bright fortnight (*śuklapakṣa*), the lunar phase of wealth (*dhanapakṣa*), and proceeds further in sequence;

likewise, during the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇa*), he goes from the lotus of the feet up to the lotus of the navel. Indeed, in the heart and the head, there are the eight-spoked and sixteen-spoked wheels known as the black and white lotuses;

at the throat is the thirty-two-spoked wheel, and another double that number at the navel, which is red and yellow. On the eighth days, the [moon] is white and black at the navel and throat, and white and black at the head and heart. || 74 ||

The first thirty vowels, joined with *ha*, *ya*, *ra*, *va*, and *la*, and differentiated by the nasal dot (*bindu*) and the venerable visarga, become sixty; these are the twenty-one hundred [petals] which, divided by the groups beginning with *ka* and differentiated by the forms of the *bindu* and *visarga* on the tips of the filaments, rise and wane according to the movement of the sun during the watches of the day. || 75 ||

Furthermore, in the case of Kṛṣṇa, likewise on the side of the debt (ṛṇapakṣa), by means of withdrawal (saṃhāra) either in the forward order as before or in reverse order, [the breath] reaches the heart of the Kṛṣṇa-padas once the debt is full. This is the rule for the *padas*.

Here, regarding the lotuses: there is an eight-spoked lotus in the heart for Kṛṣṇa, a sixteen-spoked white one in the head; at the throat is a thirty-two-spoked red one, and another double that, a sixty-four-spoked yellow one, in the navel—this is the rule for the lotus petals.

In the *Vimalaprabhā*, the locations of the four lunar nodes (*parva*) are now described, beginning with the words "the two eighths" (*dvayaṣṭamyau*), etc. Regarding the internal [system]: here, within the heart-lotus and other centers, which possess the natures of the elements wind, fire, water, and earth, the Moon moves through the pericarp and the tips of the filaments by means of the differentiation of vowels.

There are thirty initial vowels; when these are divided by the horse (*ha*), elephant (*ya*), horse (*ra*), and elephant (*la*)—that is, the short vowels (*laghu*)—along with the dots (*bindu*) and the glorious visargas (*visarga*), they become sixty.

Here, the previously mentioned five short vowels, the five in the form of *guṇas*, and the five short vowels resulting from the substitution of *yaṇ*—these fifteen, when divided by the dots (*bindu*), become thirty.
The fifteen letters beginning with *ha*, which occupy the positions of long, augmented, and protracted vowels, become thirty when divided by the visarga; thus they became sixty, as it is said:
"They are the kings of the ages (*yuga*), the Vasus, and the teeth, located on the tips of the filaments."

Here, in the heart-lotus, the Moon, having made the new moon (*amā*), moves through the thirty vowels over fifteen lunar days (*tithi*) by means of the division of the first and second halves of each day.

Here, in the heart-lotus, on the first day of the bright fortnight (*śukla-pratipad*), there is *a* in the first half and *aṃ* in the second half of the filament-tip; on the second day, *i* in the first half and *ī* in the second half—thus four pairs [of vowels] are in the heart, excluding the pericarp (*kaṇikā*).
Then, in the filament-tip of the throat-lotus, on the third day, there are *ṛ* and *ṝ* in the first and second halves respectively.

Thus, on the fourth [tithi], *u* and *ū*; on the fifth, *ḷ* and *laṃ*; on the sixth, *a* and *aṃ*; on the seventh, *e* and *eṃ*. On the eighth, *ara* is at the tip of the filaments in the first half, and *araṃ* is in the pericarp (*kaṇikā*) in the second half; thus, on the ninth, *o* and *oṃ*. On the tenth, *ala* and *alaṃ*—thus it moves through the tips of the filaments in the throat-lotus. Then, on the eleventh, *ha* and *haṃ* are in the first and second halves respectively at the tip of the filaments in the forehead-lotus; on the twelfth, *ya* and *yaṃ* in the first and second halves; on the thirteenth, *ra* and *raṃ*; on the fourteenth, *va* and *vaṃ*. On the full moon day (*pūrṇā*), *la* is at the tip of the filaments in the first half, and *laṃ* is in the pericarp in the second half.
In the head, the full moon moves through the lotus-seeds of air, fire, water, and earth according to the order of emanation (*sṛṣṭikrama*);
thereafter, during the dark fortnight, it moves through the lotus-seeds of earth according to the order of withdrawal (*saṃhārakrama*) as long vowels with the visarga.
For example: on the first day of the dark fortnight, *lāḥ* in the first half and *lā* in the second half.

Thus, in the second [petal] is *vāḥ* or *vā*; in the third, *rāḥ* or *rā*; in the fourth, *yāḥ* or *yā*; in the fifth, *hāḥ* or *hā*; in the sixth, *ālaḥ* or *āla*; in the seventh, *auḥ* or *au*; in the eighth, *āraḥ*; in the pericarp (*kaṇikā*), *āra*; in the ninth, *aiḥ* or *ai*; in the tenth, *āḥ* or *ā*; in the eleventh, *lū*; in the twelfth, *ūḥ* or *ū*; in the thirteenth, *ṛḥ* or *ṛ*; in the fourteenth, *īḥ* or *i*; and in the fifteenth, *āḥ* or *ā*. Here, in the pericarp, there are two voids (*śūnyaka*); in these two [voids], there are no vowels or visargas in the pericarp.

Furthermore, at the end of the new moon (amāvāsyā) in the heart-lotus, beginning from the first lunar day (pratipad), there is a white [digit] on the tip of the filaments of the heart-lotus and a black one; this is the rule for the eighth day of the bright fortnight (śuklāṣṭamī). On the eighth day of the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇāṣṭamī), [the digits reside] on the tip of the filaments and in the pericarp (kaṇikā) of the throat-lotus. In the navel-lotus, [they reside] on the tip of the filaments and in the pericarp; the full digit (pūrṇā) is in the heart, and the end of the full digit is in the head. Thus, the rule is that "in the heart" refers to the time of entry into the first lunar day at the conclusion of the new moon.

Now, the enjoyments of the solar signs (*sūryavyañjanabhoga*) are described with the words beginning with "bindu" and so forth: here, the consonant groups beginning with *ka* are divided by the four—namely, the *bindus*, the forms of *ā*, and the *visargas*—and thus become one hundred and twenty syllables. That very [number] rises and wanes upon the one hundred and twenty petals of the excellent lotus, according to the movement of the watches (*prahara*) through the distinction of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) and emanation (*sṛṣṭi*). Here, the "movement of the watches" refers to the four junctions (*sandhyā*); by virtue of their movement—that is, by virtue of the movement of the watches—in this heart-lotus, up to the end of the new moon (*amāvāsyā*), on the sixty-four petals starting from the first day of the lunar fortnight (*pratipad*), four petals are empty.

Among those, the *pratipad* days are as follows: *ssāḥ ssāḥ* and *yāḥ yāḥ* in the four-petaled [lotuses], representing the four twilights (*catuḥsandhyā*). Thus, on the second day, they are *ṣṣāḥ ṣṣāḥ* and *śśāḥ śśāḥ*;
likewise, on the third day, they are *kkāḥ kkāḥ* and *ttāḥ ttāḥ*.

There is no division [by vowels or visarga] in the chapter [on the signs of death and the severance of the channels]. This is the Great Section on the Signs of Death and the Severance of the Channels. In the fourth [day], *thāḥ thā*, *ddāḥ ddā*;
in the fifth, *dhdhāḥ dhdhā*, *nnāḥ nnā*.
On the sixth [day], *ppāḥ* and *ppā*, *phphāḥ* and *phphā*;
on the seventh, *bbāḥ* and *bbā*, *bbhāḥ* and *bbhā*;
on the eighth, *mmāḥ* and *mmā*, *ṭṭāḥ* and *ṭṭā*.
On the ninth day, [the syllables] are *ṭṭhāḥ* and *ṭṭhā*, *ḍḍāḥ* and *ḍḍā*;
on the tenth day, *ḍhḍhāḥ* and *ḍhḍhā*, *ṇṇāḥ* and *ṇṇā*;
and on the eleventh day, *ccāḥ* and *ccā*, *chchāḥ* and *chchā*.
On the twelfth day: *jjāḥ* and *jjā*, *jhjhāḥ* and *jhjhā*;
on the thirteenth day: *ññāḥ* and *ññā*, *kkāḥ* and *kkā*;
on the fourteenth day: *khkhāḥ* and *khkhā*, *ggāḥ* and *ggā*.
On the full moon day of the bright fortnight, at the petals of the navel-lotus, the sun, having consumed the letters of the *sa*-group— *ghghāḥ ghghā*, *ṅṅāḥ ṅṅā*— returns; thus,
by its own movement, the moon enters the head.

Then the moon comes to the lotus released by the sun, and the sun goes to the lotuses occupied by the moon; in the dark fortnight, this occurs through the process of emanation (*sṛṣṭi*) for the sun and through the process of withdrawal (*saṃhāra*) for the moon.
Here, everywhere, there is a fixed rule: when the moon moves by way of emanation, then the sun is by way of withdrawal; when the sun is by way of emanation, then the moon is by way of withdrawal.

Now, on the petals of the forehead-lotus and so forth, the Sun moves through the letters of the *ṅa*-group and other groups in reverse order: on the first day of the dark fortnight (*kṛṣṇapratipad*), he moves through *ṅa* and *ṅaṃ*, *gha* and *ghaṃ* on the four petals of the forehead; on the second day, *ga* and *gaṃ*, *kha* and *khaṃ*; on the third day, *ka* and *kaṃ*, *ña* and *ñaṃ*; and on the fourth day, *jha* and *jhaṃ*, *ja* and *jaṃ*.

Then, on the petals of the throat-lotus: on the fifth [tithi], *cha chaṃ* and *ca caṃ*; on the sixth, *ṇa ṇaṃ* and *ḍha ḍhaṃ*; on the seventh, *ḍa ḍaṃ* and *ṭha ṭhaṃ*; on the eighth, *ṭa ṭaṃ* and *ma maṃ*; on the ninth, *bha bhaṃ* and *ba baṃ*; on the tenth, *pha phaṃ* and *pa paṃ*; on the eleventh, *na naṃ* and *dha dhaṃ*; on the twelfth, *da daṃ* and *tha thaṃ*; on the thirteenth, *ta taṃ* and *ka kaṃ*—these are on the petals of the heart-lotus. On the fourteenth, *śa śaṃ* and *ṣa ṣaṃ*.
Then, on the new moon day (*amāvāsya*), *ya ya~* and *sa saṃ* are on the pericarp and the tips of the filaments.
The heart is the unstruck (*anāhata*) within the *amānta*, the void-bindu (*binduśūnya*), which is the six-syllabled [mantra];

the five-syllabled is the great void (*mahāśūnya*). This is the rule for the moon and sun. Now, the debt and credit of the moon and sun are described starting with the words "the moon" and so forth: "In a fortnight (*pakṣa*), the moon creates a debt through its own movements called 'days'; moreover, by another two months, one further day increases due to the conjunction of the year."
When the year is complete, there shall be six days; likewise it increases further until the limit of death. Thus, O King, this debt of the Sun increases twofold year after year. (76)

In this system, because of the rule that "in the constant value of the lunar day (tithi-dhruvaka), [the correction] is to be added and subtracted, and then added again" every day, a *kalā* consisting of sixty *ghaṭikās* is added to the place of the weekday (*vāra*).

Due to its being a debt, the *ghaṭikās* are subtracted from the place of *ghaṭikās*. Therefore, by a rough calculation, one *ghaṭikā* is subtracted from the *kalā* daily; by a precise calculation, it is fifty-six and a quarter *pāṇīpalas*. Why? Because when the *ahargaṇa* is divided by sixty-four, a debt results. Consequently, fifty-six and a quarter *pāṇīpalas* per day is the daily debt, which means a decrease of one *kalā* over a period of sixty-four days.

The sun [traverses] two days; likewise, during the fortnight, the moon also incurs a debt through its own movement in the station called "day" and the station called "fifteen ghaṭikās," which is the division of the lunar date (tithi) into fourth parts. The Tibetan sequence is as follows: "In the dark fortnight, by the order of the sun's increase, and by the order of the moon's decrease."
In the *Vimalaprabhā*,

by the word "and" (*ca*), it is indicated that there is a further daily decrease of fifty-six and a quarter *pāṇīpala*s; thus, over two months, another day becomes a debt at sixty-four days, and it increases again through the conjunction of the year.

When the year is complete, there shall be six days [of debt], lessened according to the previously mentioned rule; likewise, another [period] increases up to the limit of death—the limit of death being one hundred years. From that limit of death, a debt of five hundred and sixty-two and a half days increases; thus, O King, this double debt of the Sun increases from the hundred-year limit of death. Up to the limit of death, a debt of one thousand one hundred and twenty-five days increases. This is the rule regarding the debt.

Now, the number of years is stated according to the divisions of breath and so forth, beginning with "by six breaths" and so on: Six breaths constitute one *liptā*; sixty *pāṇīpala*s (seconds) make one *nāḍī* (minute); sixty such *nāḍīs* would form a day; thirty days make one month; six months make a solstice (*ayana*); two solstices are well known as one year. The lifespan of men, extending to a hundred years, is determined by the force of the temporal *nāḍīs* within the cycles of the four ages (*yugas*). || 77 ||

In this body of human beings, six breaths—both inhalation and exhalation—constitute one *likṣā*, and that is called a *pāṇīpala*. Sixty such *pāṇīpalas* constitute one *ghaṭikā*, which consists of one *daṇḍa*. Sixty such *nāḍīs* (ghaṭikās) would form a day and night (*ahorātra*). Thirty days, multiplied by three [fortnights], constitute one month. By ten such [months] multiplied by three, there are thirty [days] for one [month]. By those six months beginning with Capricorn, one solstice (*ayana*) occurs; that very solstice, doubled, is known as one year.

Therefore, there is no yogi in the three worlds capable of fulfilling a lifespan of a hundred years among gods, serpents, or humans. The Moon and Sun move within one's own body through the count of days; by the Moon’s own movements, he traverses all the lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*), while the Sun moves through all the asterisms in the world. Year after year, however, the hero of the Wheel of Time (*Kālacakra*) gradually swallows the world along with the earth during the course of a year.

In this triple world, among gods, serpents, and humans, there is no yogi capable of filling the moon and sun within his own body. For what reason? Because by its own movement, the moon does not traverse the three hundred and sixty-day count during the year; and the sun, until death, does not traverse all twenty-seven lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) within the year in the body, according to the previously mentioned method in the world. Therefore, year after year, it devours the world and the body through its debt; the Kālacakra hero is the cause of the production and destruction of beings—the Kālacakra hero of those who move. Thus, he must be mastered by the yogi, having filled the moon and sun with the dharma of bodhicitta and *rajas*, and having filled the prāṇa and apāna. This is the rule of the Blessed Buddha. Now, the characteristics of the transformation of the elements such as urine are stated, beginning with "if one channel is severed" (*chinnā yadyekanāḍī*): "If one channel is severed, O Lord of Men, the urine becomes like water; then, for five nights, it abandons its measure. At the time of the dissolution of the aggregate (*piṇḍa*), even the supreme digit (*kalā*) [is lost]. It emits sound in the ear, and indeed abandons taste in the mouth; the star [vision] in the center of the eyes, scent in the nose of men, and warmth in the hands and feet of the body, in succession. (79)

O King—this is an address—here in this body, if one channel, whether the left or the right, is severed and becomes devoid of the flow of the vital breath (prāṇa), then within the limit of six months, the supreme power (parakalā), which is the vital energy (prāṇa-śakti), abandons those five elements for five nights respectively. Within the limit of six days, she abandons them in due order; at the time of the dissolution of the physical body (piṇḍa) each day, she abandons the object of sound from the ear—since the word "ear" (karṇe) appears in the scriptural reading as a locative used in the sense of the ablative—and she also abandons taste.

Indeed, [the signs of death appear as follows]: the tongue in the mouth for a period of five days; the pupils in the middle of the eyes for a period of four days; the sense of smell from the nose for a period of three days; the state of heat and the state of touch in the hands, feet, and body of men for a period of two days; and on the final day, one abandons the element of dharma (dharmadhātu), the emission of semen, and the cycle of breath. Within another six days, these are declared to be the characteristics of death; on that very day, death itself occurs. || 80 ||

The tip of the nose hangs down; with arms held over the head, one's own form is seen, yet even when rubbed with lac-dye, no color appears on the palms of both hands. The sun appears black, and the full moon appears yellow. O King, when death has entered this body, the tip of one's own nose is seen hanging down like the trunk of an elephant; with arms held over the head, one sees one's own true nature, yet nothing subtle is seen. Likewise, even when rubbed with lac-dye, no color appears on the skin of the palms. The sun appears black, and the full moon—the moon at its peak—is seen as entirely yellow. This lasts for a period of six days. Then, O King, on the day when the urine and the body become cold, death occurs on that very day—this is the address. Furthermore, another sign of death within six days is stated: a black line appears beneath the tongue; a very fine Brahma-line appears in the eyes; the breath flickers through the path of the sun and moon; likewise, both cheeks [become pale]. In the *Vimalaprabhā*, regarding the internal [signs]: the entire host of planets is seen above the breasts, enveloped in the armpits and accompanied by sparks; the neck is stiff, the limbs are rigid, and there is even a whirling sensation in the body—these are the signs of the eighth-day death. (81)

In this world, for one overcome by the signs of death (*ariṣṭamaraṇa*), a black line like the "thread of time" (*kālasūtra*) appears beneath the tongue; likewise, in the eyes, an extremely fine line the measure of a hair, which pierces the circles of black and red, appears above the *brahmarandhra*. The breath flickers through the paths of the moon and sun; both cheeks throb; likewise, the two channels (*nāḍī*) reach up to the armpits and the breasts; the entire host of planets is no longer seen, or is seen emitting sparks; his neck, limbs, hands, and feet become stiff and motionless; even wandering occurs within his body. These eight characteristics of death have been declared. Furthermore, whatever else is seen as contrary—whether in the body or externally, such as the shadow-person (*chāyāpuruṣa*) and so forth—all that should be understood by the yogi as a sign of death. Having known that, acts such as giving (*dāna*) should be performed. Even if he lives by the power of merit, it is still auspicious; and if he goes to death, he nevertheless experiences the fruit of what was given. Therefore, gifts should be given from both sides by followers of the Sugata who desire happiness; such is the rule of the Blessed One. Thus ends the fourth great chapter, the Great Chapter on the Characteristics of Death and Signs of Death, the Severing of the Channels, the Characteristics of Moments, and the Rule of Kālacakra, in the *Vimalaprabhā*, the twelve-thousand-verse commentary on the *Laghukālacakratantrarāja* following the *Mūlatantra*. 4.

Now, the agent characterized by creation and destruction is described according to worldly convention, beginning with the words "He who creates birth": "He who effects birth—the stage of procreation, the forms of childhood and youth—is that very one who performs destruction in the world; yet he is Kālacakrin, not the Sun. That Blessed One swallows the gods, such as the Moon and the Sun, along with all beings during the portion of night, and releases them again, even though they are infinite, during the time of day for the sake of creation, in due order. (82)

In this saṃsāra, that moment of death (*cyutikṣaṇa*) which causes the birth of sentient beings—possessing the nature of the *ālayavijñāna* and joined with *rajas* and semen—thereafter brings about the time of birth within the womb, and produces the forms of infancy, childhood, and so forth. That very moment of death is the creator and destroyer of the body; it is Kālacakra in the world who performs [this] again in heaven, the mortal realm, and the netherworld (*pātāla*), and not the sun. The meaning is this: the sun is *rajas* and the moon is semen; without the *ālayavijñāna*, and without Kālacakra, [the sun and moon] do not perform [this function]. Why does he not perform [this] here? It is said that the statement "the world everywhere consists of fire, sun, and moon" is well-known. Here, because he swallows the gods such as the Moon and Sun along with the elements during the portion of night, he is the Blessed One. In this saṃsāra, the portion of night is the Moon, which is creation (*sṛṣṭi*); the portion of day is the Sun, which is destruction (*saṃhāra*). Here, during the portion of night at the time of origination, that which has the characteristic of the *ālayavijñāna*—[as described in] the Great Chapter on the Regulation of Kālacakra characterized by non-momentariness—is the Moon as semen within the mother’s womb, and the Sun as *rajas*. By the word "etcetera," he swallows those produced from feces and urine, together with the elements of earth, water, fire, air, and space, while remaining in the support of *rajas* and semen for the sake of producing body, speech, and mind. The Moon is semen, the Lord (*īśvara*); *rajas* is the Sun, Sadāśiva; marrow is Rudra; urine is Viṣṇu; and feces is Brahmā.
During the portion of night at the time of arising, it swallows the moon, sun, and other deities;
